merges.sentence: The university sets no single AI policy and leaves AI-use decisions to faculty.
merges.why: All state the institution avoids one-size-fits-all rules and defers AI decisions to instructors.

merges.sentence: Teaching assistants and staff use AI in their roles only as the instructor authorizes.
merges.why: All make TA and staff AI use conditional on instructor or supervisor permission.

merges.sentence: Administrators or designated offices review AI tools for security, privacy and compliance before approving them.
merges.why: All describe a pre-adoption review and approval of AI tools by a designated office.

merges.sentence: The university maintains and publishes a list of approved AI tools.
merges.why: Both state the institution keeps and communicates a list of approved tools.

merges.sentence: Administrators regularly reassess deployed AI systems for performance, accuracy, security and compliance.
merges.why: Both require ongoing post-deployment assessment of AI systems.

merges.sentence: Designated offices monitor and audit campus AI use for compliance.
merges.why: Both describe institutional auditing of AI use to check compliance.

merges.sentence: Administrators may block or disable unauthorized or risky AI tools.
merges.why: Both grant administrators the power to block AI tools.

merges.sentence: Staff acquire AI tools only through the university's standard procurement process.
merges.why: Both require standard procurement and contracting for AI purchases.

merges.sentence: A named body regularly reviews and updates the AI policy and guidance.
merges.why: All describe scheduled or ongoing review and updating of the policy by a responsible body.

merges.sentence: The AI policy is interim or under development, and fuller policy is forthcoming.
merges.why: Both state the current policy is provisional with more to come.

merges.sentence: Policy documents state their publication and revision dates and version history.
merges.why: Both describe the document listing its dates and update history.

merges.sentence: Administrators gather community feedback and survey input to inform AI policy.
merges.why: Both collect input from the campus community to shape policy.

merges.sentence: Administrators establish standing AI committees or councils to address AI issues.
merges.why: Both describe creating standing bodies to handle AI.

merges.sentence: The institution provides faculty with AI training, workshops, consultations and support.
merges.why: All describe institutional AI professional development for faculty.

merges.sentence: The institution offers AI courses, workshops and resources to its whole community.
merges.why: Both describe community-wide AI training and resources.

merges.sentence: The institution integrates AI literacy into curricula so students use AI responsibly.
merges.why: All describe building AI literacy into the curriculum to prepare students.

merges.sentence: Teaching assistants, staff and administrators stay informed about evolving AI developments.
merges.why: Both ask the same actors to keep current on AI developments.

merges.sentence: Colleges, departments and programs may set their own discipline-specific AI rules.
merges.why: All state that units develop their own AI policies or expectations.

merges.sentence: Administrators publish baseline principles and a shared framework for generative AI use.
merges.why: Both establish institution-wide baseline AI principles.

merges.sentence: The university commits to equitable, inclusive access to AI tools for everyone.
merges.why: Both state a commitment to equitable AI access.

merges.sentence: AI tools and systems must meet accessibility standards.
merges.why: Both apply accessibility requirements to AI systems.

merges.sentence: The university encourages AI use to improve administrative efficiency.
merges.why: Both promote AI for efficiency in operations.

merges.sentence: Staff disclose how they use AI in their work and materials.
merges.why: Both require staff transparency about their own AI use.

merges.sentence: The university provides no AI detection tool.
merges.why: Both state the institution offers no AI detector.

merges.sentence: Administrators update honor codes and conduct policies to cover generative AI.
merges.why: Both call for revising honor codes in response to AI.

merges.sentence: Misconduct processes favor educational responses over punitive charges.
merges.why: Both describe educational, supportive handling of AI misconduct.

merges.sentence: Universities build their AI guidance on peer institutions' policies.
merges.why: Both draw on other institutions' policies when developing guidance.

merges.sentence: Departments and administrators review learning outcomes in light of AI.
merges.why: Both call for reviewing learning goals because of AI.
